U6-00582: A freed slave-woman belonging to Maymunah was given a sheep as charity, and it died. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by it and said,
"Why did you not take its hide, tan it, and benefit from it?"
They said, "It is carrion." He said,
Abū Bakr and Ibn Abī ʿUmar said in their narrations, from Maymunah, may Allah be pleased with her
U6-01446: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Accept this invitation when you are invited to it."
He said: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar would attend invitations, whether to a wedding or otherwise, and he would attend them even while fasting.
U6-01323: Ibn ʿAbbās used to say, "No pilgrim or non-pilgrim circumambulates the House except that he thereby becomes lawful again (released from the restrictions of ihram)."

I said to ʿAṭāʾ, "From where does he derive that?" He said, "From the words of Allah, the Exalted: {Then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House}." I said, "But that is after the standing at ʿArafah."
He replied, "Ibn ʿAbbās used to say it is after the standing at ʿArafah and before it."
He derived this from the Prophet's ﷺ command when he instructed them to exit ihram during the Farewell Pilgrimage.
U6-00321: Muʿādh used to pray with the Prophet ﷺ and then go to his people and lead them in prayer. One night he prayed the ʿishāʾ with the Prophet ﷺ, then went to his people and led them, beginning with Sūrat al-Baqarah. A man broke away, prayed alone, and departed. They said to him, "You have become a hypocrite, so-and-so!" He said, "No, by Allah, I will go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and inform him."

He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we are people who work water-drawing camels during the day, and Muʿādh prayed with you the ʿishāʾ, then came and began with Sūrat al-Baqarah."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to Muʿādh and said,
"O Muʿādh, are you a source of trouble? Recite such-and-such, and such-and-such."
Sufyān said: I said to ʿAmr that Abū al-Zubayr had narrated to us from Jābir that he said:
"Recite: By the sun and its brightness. And the morning brightness.
By the night when it covers.
And glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High."
U6-00895: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us, three hundred riders, with Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ as our commander, to intercept a caravan of Quraysh. We camped on the coast for half a month, and severe hunger struck us until we ate al-khabaṭ (leaves of trees), so the army was named the Army of Khabaṭ. The sea cast up to us a creature called al-ʿanbar, and we ate from it for half a month and anointed ourselves with its fat until our bodies regained their strength. He said: Abū ʿUbaydah took one of its ribs and set it up, then looked at the tallest man in the army and the tallest camel, and had him pass under it. He said: Men sat in the socket of its eye, and we extracted from the hollow of its eye so-and-so many bowls of fat. He said: We had with us a sack of dates, and Abū ʿUbaydah would give each one of us a handful, then gave us one date each. When it ran out, we felt its absence.
U6-01474: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the two who had performed mutual cursing (li'ān),
"Your reckoning is with Allah; one of you is a liar. You have no further claim over her."
The man said, "O Messenger of Allah, what about my property?"
He said, "You have no property. If you spoke truthfully about her, then it was for what you made lawful of her private part; and if you lied about her, then that puts her further beyond your reach."
Zuhayr said in his narration: Sufyān narrated to us from ʿAmr, who heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say, 'I heard Ibn ʿUmar say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:'
U6-01149: I kept company with Abū Hurayrah for five years, and I heard him narrate
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"The Children of Israel were led by prophets.
Whenever a prophet died, another prophet succeeded him.
Indeed, there will be no prophet after me,
and there will be caliphs, and they will be many.
They asked, "What then do you command us?" He said, "Fulfill the pledge to the first, then the first, and give them their rights,
for Allah will hold them accountable for what He entrusted to them."
U6-01524: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "My brother has diarrhea."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Give him honey."
He gave him honey, then came back and said, "I gave him honey, but it only increased his diarrhea."
The Prophet ﷺ said that to him three times. Then he came the fourth time, and he said, "Give him honey."
He said, "I gave him honey, but it only increased his diarrhea."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Allah has spoken the truth, and your brother's belly has lied." So he gave him honey, and he was cured.
U6-01421: Three men came to the homes of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ asking about the worship of the Prophet ﷺ. When they were informed of it, they considered it little and said, "Where are we in relation to the Prophet ﷺ, for Allah has forgiven him what preceded of his sins and what followed?"
One of them said, "As for me, I pray at night forever."
Another said, "I fast continually and never break my fast."
Another said, "I withdraw from women and will never marry."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to them and said, "
"You are the ones who said such-and-such. By Allah, I am the most fearful of Allah among you and the most mindful of Him,
but I fast and I break my fast,
I pray and I sleep, and I marry women.
Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."
U6-00145: The Prophet ﷺ would go around to all his wives in one hour of the night or the day,
He said: I asked Anas ibn Mālik, "Was he able to manage that?" He replied, "We used to say that he was given the strength of thirty men."
Saʿīd reported from Qatādah that Anas ibn Mālik had told them of nine women.
U6-01342: from the hypocrites in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever the Prophet ﷺ went out to battle, they would stay behind from him and rejoice at their remaining behind in opposition to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Prophet ﷺ returned, they would make excuses to him and swear oaths, and they loved to be praised for what they had not done. Then the verse was revealed: "Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought and love to be praised for what they did not do are safe from punishment."
U6-00029: A man from the Jews came to ʿUmar and said, "O Commander of the Faithful, there is a verse in your Book that you recite. If it had been revealed to us, the Jews, we would have taken that day as a festival."

He said, "Which verse?" The man said: "Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and approved Islam as your religion." ʿUmar said, "I know the day it was revealed and the place where it was revealed. It was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at ʿArafāt on a Friday."
U6-01032: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has not barred me from him since I embraced Islam, and he has never seen me without smiling in my face.
Ibn Numayr added in his narration from Ibn Idrīs: "I complained to him that I could not stay firm on horses, so he struck my chest with his hand and said, "
"O Allah, make him steadfast, and make him a guide who is guided."
U6-00570: Some people from the Ansār asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and whoever of them asked him received what he gave, until what he had was exhausted. When everything was spent, he said to them, as he gave freely with his hands, "
Whatever good I have, I will not store up from you.
Whoever seeks to be chaste, Allah will keep him chaste;
whoever seeks patience, Allah will grant him patience;
whoever seeks independence, Allah will make him independent;
and you will never be given a gift better or more expansive than patience."
U6-01217: When ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was placed on his bier, people surrounded him, supplicating, praising him, and invoking blessings upon him before he was lifted. I was among them. He said: Then I was startled by a man who had taken hold of my shoulder from behind. I turned and it was ʿAlī. He invoked mercy upon ʿUmar and said, "You have left behind no one more beloved to me to meet Allah with his deeds than you. By Allah, I truly thought that Allah would place you with your two companions, for I often heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, "
I came with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, entered with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, and left with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar."
For indeed, I was hoping, or thinking, that Allah would place you with them.
U6-00515: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah fell ill, so the Prophet ﷺ came to visit him along with ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with them. When he entered upon him and found him surrounded by his family, he said, "He has died."
They said, "No, O Messenger of Allah."
The Prophet ﷺ wept, and when the people saw the Prophet ﷺ weeping, they wept. Then he said, "
Do you not hear that Allah does not punish for the tears of the eye,
nor for the grief of the heart,
but He punishes for this (pointing to his tongue), or He has mercy. Indeed, the dead are punished for their families' weeping over them."
ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, would strike [those who wailed] with a staff,
and would throw stones and scatter dust.
U6-00421: one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day to pray for rain. He turned his back to the people, supplicated Allah while facing the qiblah, turned his cloak inside out, and then prayed two rakʿahs.
U6-01583: asked permission to enter upon the Prophet ﷺ. When he saw him, he said:
'What an evil brother of the clan,
and what an evil son of the clan.'
When the man sat down, the Prophet ﷺ received him with a cheerful face and was cordial with him,
and when the man left, ʿĀʾishah said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, when you saw the man, you said such-and-such to him,
then you received him with a cheerful face and were cordial with him.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
'O ʿĀʾishah, when have you known me to be obscene?
Indeed, the most evil of people in status with Allah on the Day of Resurrection is the one whom people leave alone to avoid his evil.'
U6-01927: Ḥujr — Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said, 'He informed us,' whereas the others said, 'He narrated to us': Ismāʿīl
— i.e., Ibn Jaʿfar — from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār,
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Whoever keeps a dog, other than a hunting dog or a herding dog, his good deeds decrease by two qīrāṭs every day.'
U6-01944: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār was told that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
'Every prophet has a supplication he makes, but I intend, God willing, to keep my supplication as an intercession for my community on the Day of Resurrection.'
Kaʿb said to Abū Hurayrah, 'Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?' Abū Hurayrah said, 'Yes.'
U6-01945: From the Prophet ﷺ that he said:
'A servant's supplication will continue to be answered as long as he does not pray for sin or the severing of ties of kinship, and as long as he does not become hasty.'
It was asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is haste?' He said:
'He says, I have supplicated and supplicated, yet I see that I am not answered, and so he becomes despondent and abandons supplication.'
U6-01892: Saʿīd said: There was something between Khālid ibn al-Walīd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, so Khālid insulted him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Do not insult any of my Companions. For if one of you were to spend gold equal to Mount Uḥud, he would not reach the mudd of any one of them, nor even half of it.'
U6-01810: A prayer in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except in al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the last of the Prophets and his mosque is the last of the mosques.

Abū Salamah and Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: We had no doubt that Abū Hurayrah was reporting a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but that prevented us from asking Abū Hurayrah to verify that hadith, until Abū Hurayrah passed away. Then we discussed it and blamed ourselves for not having asked Abū Hurayrah about it, so that he could attribute it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ if he had heard it from him. While we were in that state, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Qāriẓ sat with us, and we mentioned that hadith and our neglect in not confirming its wording from Abū Hurayrah. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ibrāhīm said to us, 'I testify that I heard Abū Hurayrah say, The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:'
'Indeed I am the last of the Prophets, and indeed my mosque is the last of the mosques.'
U6-01828: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only performed the sa'y around the House and between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah in order to show the polytheists his strength.
Al-Ḥumaydī added: Sufyān related to us, ʿAmr related to us, I heard ʿAṭāʾ,
U6-01942: While we were travelling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-ʿArj, a poet appeared reciting poetry. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Seize the devil, or restrain the devil, for a man's belly being filled with pus is better for him than being filled with poetry.'
U6-01804: A year of drought struck the people during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was delivering the sermon on the pulpit on Friday, a Bedouin stood up and said, “O Messenger of Allah,”
property has perished and dependents are hungry,
so supplicate to Allah for us that He give us rain.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands,
and there was not a cloud in the sky.
He said: Then clouds gathered like mountains
and he did not come down from his pulpit until I saw the rain flowing down upon his beard.
He said: We were given rain that day,
and the next day, and the day after it, and the one following, until the next Friday.
Then that Bedouin, or another man, stood up and said, “O Messenger of Allah,”
the buildings have collapsed and the property has been flooded,
so supplicate to Allah for us.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands and said,
“O Allah, around us and not upon us.”
He said: He did not point with his hand toward any part of the sky except that it cleared, until Madinah was like a basin in the midst of the sky,
until the Wadi Qanāh flowed for a month.
He said: No one arrived from any direction without reporting the heavy rain.
U6-01910: Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul used to say to a slave girl of his, “Go and seek something for us for us.” So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: “And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution if they desire chastity, in order to seek the commodities of worldly life. And whoever compels them, indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful.”
U6-01871: Anas ibn Mālik related to us from Abū Ṭalḥah,
that the Prophet ﷺ ordered on the day of Badr that twenty-four men from the chiefs of Quraysh be thrown into one of the wells of Badr, a vile and rotting carcass.
Whenever he gained victory over a people, he would stay on the battlefield for three nights.
When he was at Badr on the third day,
he ordered his mount to be brought, and its saddle fastened.
Then he walked, and his Companions followed him, saying, “We think he is only going out for some need,”
until he stood at the edge of the well.
He began calling them by their names and their fathers’ names:
and O so-and-so son of so-and-so,
would it please you that you had obeyed Allah and His Messenger? Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true,
so have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?”
He said: Umar said, “O Messenger of Allah,
how can you speak to bodies that have no spirits in them?” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad,
you do not hear what I say any better than they do.”
Qatādah said: Allah brought them back to life so that they could hear His words as rebuke, humiliation, retribution, anguish and remorse.
U6-05497: Qays said: Tamīm al-Dārī came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him that he had boarded the sea, and his ship had gone astray, so he was cast onto an island. He went out to it seeking water and met a person trailing his hair.
He related the hadith, and in it he said: Then he said, “As for me, if I had been permitted to go out, I would have trodden every land except Ṭaybah.”
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ brought him out to the people and related it to them. He said,
“This is Ṭaybah, and that is the Dajjal.”
U6-02007: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Khaybar.
When we reached al-Ṣahbāʾ (Yaḥyā said: it is an afternoon’s journey from Khaybar), he asked for food, but only sawīq was brought.
so we moistened it and ate with him.
Then he asked for water, rinsed his mouth, and we rinsed our mouths with him.
Then he led us in the Maghrib prayer and did not perform ablution again.
Sufyān said: It is as if you heard it from Yaḥyā.
U6-05152: Al-Bunānī and Sulaymān al-Taymī related from Anas ibn Mālik
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“I came upon Mūsā (and in a narration from Hudhāb, “I passed by Mūsā”) on the night of my Night Journey, near the red sand hill, while he was standing and praying in his grave.”
U6-02549: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The best of you is my generation,
ʿImrān said: I do not know whether he mentioned after two or three generations. The Prophet ﷺ said:
“After you there will be a people who betray and are not trusted, who bear witness without being asked to,
and who make vows but do not fulfill them,
U6-04808: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

There is no raiding party that goes out in the cause of Allah and obtains booty, except that they receive two-thirds of their reward in advance from the Hereafter, and one-third remains for them. But if they obtain no booty, their full reward is credited to them.
U6-02108: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
Listen and obey, even if an Abyssinian slave with a head like a raisin is appointed over you.
U6-03315: With this same [report], she said: The Prophet ﷺ came in to me one day and said:
O ʿĀʾishah, I do not think that so-and-so and so-and-so understand our religion, which we follow.
U6-02059: went out from the presence of the Prophet ﷺ on a dark night,
and there was a light before them until they parted,
and the light went with them.
Muʿammar said, from Thābit, from Anas, that Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr and a man from the Anṣār
U6-03219: I was a guest of Abū Hurayrah for seven [nights],
and he, his wife, and his servant would alternate the night into thirds: one would pray,
then he would wake this one.
I also heard him say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ distributed dates among his Companions,
and I received seven dates, one of which was a dry, shriveled date.
U6-04117: That a son of his had died at Quddayd or ʿUsfān, and he said, “O Kurayb, look at how many people have gathered for him.”
He said: I went out and found that people had gathered for him, so I informed him, and he said, “Do you say they are forty?” He said, “Yes.”
U6-04668: Whenever revelation came down upon the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, he would be overcome with distress and his face would darken. [He said:] Then one day it descended upon him and he experienced that again; when it lifted from him, he said:

Take from me, take from me. Allah has made a way for them: the married with the married, and the virgin with the virgin. The married person receives a hundred lashes and then is stoned, and the virgin receives a hundred lashes and then is exiled for a year.
U6-05232: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said that about a month or so before his death:
“There is no soul created today that will still be alive a hundred years from now.”
the keeper of the water supply, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh,
from the Prophet ﷺ in similar terms. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān explained it, saying, “It means the reduction of the lifespan.”
U6-03752: I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān, and I never heard any of them recite “In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.”
U6-05208: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
Satirize the Quraysh, for it is harder on them than a volley of arrows.
Then he sent for Ibn Rawāḥah and said, “Satirize them.”

So he satirized them, but he was not satisfied. Then he sent for Kaʿb ibn Mālik, and then sent for Ḥassān ibn Thābit. When he came in to him, Ḥassān said, “The time has come for you to send for this lion that strikes with its tail,” and he stuck out his tongue and began moving it, and said, “By the One who sent you with truth, I will tear them apart with my tongue as a tanned hide is cut.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Do not hurry. Abū Bakr is the most knowledgeable of Quraysh about their lineages, and I have kinship among them. Go to him until he makes my lineage clear to you.”

So Ḥassān went to him, then returned and said, “O Messenger of Allah, he has made your lineage clear to me. By the One who sent you with truth, I will extract you from them just as a hair is pulled from dough.”
U6-05538: ʿĀʾishah said to me, O nephew, they were commanded to seek forgiveness
for the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, so they reviled them.
U6-03922: Our homes were distant from the mosque,
our houses so we could come closer to the mosque, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us and said:
“Indeed, for you there is a rank for every step.”
U6-03784: The Prophet ﷺ led us in the dawn prayer in Makkah, beginning Sūrat al-Muʾminūn until he reached the mention of Mūsā and Hārūn, or the mention of ʿĪsā—Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād is unsure, or they differed about it—when the Prophet ﷺ was seized by a fit of coughing, so he bowed, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Sāʾib was present for that.
In the narration of ʿAbd al-Razzāq, he cut it short and bowed.
In his narration: and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr.
And he did not say Ibn al-ʿĀṣ.
